196rbbl: With the pluperfect subjunctive you express regret or sorrow about something that can no longer be changed. Compare the three kinds of «ojalá»: with the present, the wish is possible («ojalá ganemos»); with the imperfect, it is difficult in the present («ojalá tuviéramos un bote nuevo»); with the pluperfect, it is impossible because the past is closed («ojalá hubiéramos ganado»).
1ro1itf: Other useful expressions of regret: «¡quién hubiera dicho…!», «me habría gustado que…», «lástima que no hubiéramos…». To avoid overdramatising, follow the regret with a proposal: «ojalá hubiéramos entrenado con viento; la próxima vez lo haremos».

7rrk6u: Original SpanishCue text written as a letter from a fictional rowing club in Santa Fe. The people and results are invented.
xl4o05: Dear team: the season is over and I want to thank you for your effort before talking about results. We came second in the regional final, eight tenths of a second behind first place. I know many of you went home thinking about those eight tenths. So did I. But second place is not a failure, and I ask you to look at it with a cool head.
1i8ixis: I'll start with what didn't go well. If we had checked the order of the heats on Friday, we would have known that we were due to start in the wind. Nobody did, and I am the one most responsible. I also believe that, if we had practised more starts during the winter, we wouldn't have lost so much ground in the first few metres. It hurt me that some of you blamed each other on the jetty, because we lost the race together.
1ck8gz0: Now, what went well. I was moved that Paula, who couldn't row, had travelled anyway to help with the boat and cheer from the shore. I was pleasantly surprised that the youngest rowers had learned in just a few months to coordinate their strokes with the rest. And I was glad that, the next day, nobody missed training.
1kfbpu1: I also want to be fair to the Rosario team. They won because they rowed better in the final stretch, not through luck. Their coach told me afterwards that they had spent the whole winter practising in a crosswind. If we had done the same, the margin would probably have been different. I'm not saying this so that we feel sorry for ourselves, but because it is the most useful piece of information the final left us with.
1azjvmk: Would we have won with different preparation? Maybe, maybe not. If only we had had another chance that same afternoon, but regattas aren't rerun. What we can do is use this experience. That's why I propose three changes: checking the official programme two days in advance, practising starts once a week and training on windy days, even if they are uncomfortable. See you on Monday in the shed.
